subject: Request: Key zeroization & delegated KMS access - onboarding plan
messages:
From: Teresa Lin <security@novushealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ken Morales <procurement@novushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifications on BYOK, zeroization and delegated KMS access for onboarding

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the RFP responses — overall helpful. Before we proceed to the security review board, we need a concise plan addressing three items so our InfoSec & Procurement teams can greenlight the onboarding:

1) Key zeroization: If we provide customer-managed keys (BYOK) during onboarding, what is Redwood's process for zeroizing those keys from any transient systems after activation? We need explicit timelines and evidence types you can provide (logs, signed attestation, nonce-based proofs).

2) Delegated KMS access model: We want to allow a small set of Novus engineers to perform key rotations without Redwood exposing key material. Can you describe the delegated access model (roles, API scopes, audit events) and whether you support short-lived credentials or just long-term roles?

3) TLS & cipher requirements: Our policy requires TLS 1.3 + a minimum cipher profile and forward secrecy. Do you enforce server-side TLS profiles (e.g., disallow RSA key exchange) and can you provide cipher lists used by your public and private endpoints?

We have a procurement deadline of Aug 30; if you can get a short answer set and supporting artifacts this week, that would keep us on track.

Thanks,
Teresa Lin
Security Architect, Novus Health

Attachment: novus-questionnaire-template.xlsx (referenced)

Hi Teresa — thanks for the clear list. Putting Marissa and Dev on the thread for technical detail; below is a high-level mutual action plan so Procurement/InfoSec know next steps.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Today: Redwood provides a one-page bulleted answer + two artifacts (onboarding playbook, latest HSM attestation).
- Mon (Aug 23): Technical deep-dive call (30 min) with your InfoSec + our infra team; Marissa will lead.
- Tue (Aug 24): Provide sample audit logs and a redacted zeroization attestation template for Novus to review.
- By Aug 27: Confirm delegated KMS access SLAs and Flow (role mappings + time-limited credential options).

Quick answers (high level):
- Zeroization: We support immediate zeroization upon written request. Transient key material is never stored outside the HSM; when zeroization is requested we delete all key wrapping keys and purge cache entries; we provide a signed JSON attestation and a timestamped audit log entry.
- Delegated KMS access: We support role-based delegated actions via scoped IAM tokens (short-lived). We can offer time-limited rotation tokens (1-24 hours) for Novus operators and audit every rotation event.
- TLS: Public endpoints require TLS1.3 with AEAD ciphers and forward secrecy; private/VPC endpoints can be configured to stricter cipher suites per account.

I am attaching the onboarding playbook and the most recent HSM attestation; Marissa will follow up with the precise cipher lists and log examples.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-onboarding-playbook.pdf, hsm-attestation-2027-07.pdf

Hi Teresa,

Thanks — I ran this by infra and crypto ops. Below are the discrete answers you can share with your security board. I included examples of evidence we can provide and relevant constraints.

1) Key zeroization (BYOK import life-cycle)
- Where keys live: Customer-supplied key material is imported directly into an HSM-backed key slot in our certified HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3). We never persist unwrapped key material on disk.
- Trigger & timeline: Zeroization (full purge) is initiated on written request (email to security-requests@redwood.ai + signed PO condition). Once initiated we: 1) revoke any short-lived wrapping tokens, 2) remove key entries from HSM key slots, 3) purge in-memory caches and KV entries, and 4) record a zeroization audit event. Expected completion: < 15 minutes for single-key operations; up to 4 hours for bulk imports (we provide progress updates).
- Evidence: We provide (a) a signed attestation PDF (HSM signer + timestamp), (b) the audit log entry id(s) in our immutable log (sha256 chain link), and (c) a redacted example of the zeroization request/response flow. We can also include an ops runbook slice showing command traces (redacted).

2) Delegated KMS access model
- Model: Role-Based Delegation via account-scoped roles. Two supported modes: a) Short-lived scoped rotation tokens (recommended) issued via our token broker (1–24 hour TTL), b) Long-lived delegated roles with MFA enforced (less common).
- Capabilities: Rotations, key-version promotion, and scheduled rewraps can be scoped to the delegated role. Import/export of key material is not permitted via delegated roles; only authorized admins can initiate BYOK imports.
- Audit & controls: Every action emits an audit event with actor, role, request id, and pre/post key version hash. Audit events are cryptographically signed and stored in the immutable log for 7 years (standard) with on-request extracts for 13 months.
- Example artifacts: sample rotation API call (curl), sample audit event (redacted), and role mapping CSV.

3) TLS & cipher configurations
- Public endpoints: TLS 1.3 only; cipher suites restricted to TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256. RSA key exchange is not supported.
- Private/VPC endpoints: Customer-managed TLS profiles supported (you can supply a custom profile via the Console). We also support mutual TLS for workload authentication.
- Certificate management: We support ACME-managed certs for hosted endpoints and customer-provided certs for private endpoints; OCSP stapling is enabled.

Misc details & constraints
- HSM attestation: Attached is our last attestation (hsm-attestation-2027-07.pdf). We perform yearly attestation and will provide on-request reports during procurement.
- Logs & artifact delivery: We can provide a redacted sample audit log and a signed attestation within 48 hours after the call. For cryptographic proofs we use an HSM-signed timestamp and sha256 chain references.

Action items:
- Irene: schedule the 30-minute tech call with Novus InfoSec — propose Mon 08/23 11:00 ET or Tue 08/24 09:00 ET.
- Teresa: confirm preferred time and whether you want mutual TLS enabled for the private endpoint.

Happy to walk through any of these live; I have included sample curl snippets and an example audit extract in the drive link Irene shared.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Infrastructure & Crypto Ops, Redwood Inference
